abstract: Upwork's Future Workforce Index 2026 (July 14, 2026) documents a bifurcated freelancer market under AI: freelancers doing AI work earn 34% more per hour, but generative-AI/creative production contracts saw per-contract earnings fall 13% even as volume rose 90% YoY. Complex AI-augmented work saw earnings rise 45%; AI-augmented professional services grew 72% in volume with 22% higher earnings. Skilled freelancers now make up 38% of US knowledge workers.
keyFindings: Freelancers performing AI work earn 34% more per hour than non-AI freelancers
GenAI/creative production contracts: +90% YoY volume, -13% per-contract earnings — commoditization signal
Skilled freelancers = 38% of US knowledge workers, up from 28% (+10pp YoY)
58% of full-time employees now consider freelancing (up from 36%)
methodology: Combines proprietary Upwork marketplace transactional data with survey responses from skilled professionals across employees and freelancers. Sample size exceeds 3,000 professionals plus platform-wide contract data.
qualifiers: Upwork is the platform hosting the transactions, giving both privileged visibility and commercial incentive to frame skilled/AI-augmented freelancing favorably. Per-contract earnings decline in GenAI/creative work is a strong commoditization signal even within a self-serving report.
